entries.object: staying near Rājagaha in the Mango Grove of Jīvaka Komārabhacca

spans.text: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Mango Grove of Jīvaka Komārabhacca, together with a large Saṅgha of 1,250 mendicants.

spans.text: Now, at that time it was the sabbath—the Komudī full moon on the fifteenth day of the fourth month—and King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, was sitting upstairs in the royal longhouse surrounded by his ministers.

entries.task_id: king ajātasattu|had|women mounted on each of the five hundred female elephants
entries.description: King Ajātasattu had women mounted on each of the five hundred female elephants
entries.subject: King Ajātasattu
entries.object: women mounted on each of the five hundred female elephants

spans.text: Then King Ajātasattu had women mounted on each of the five hundred female elephants, while he mounted his bull elephant.
Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhīto saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto jīvakaṁ komārabhaccaṁ etadavoca: He said to Jīvaka, “kacci maṁ, samma jīvaka, na vañcesi?

entries.description: yaṁ tvaṁ pitaraṁ dhammikaṁ dhammarājānaṁ jīvitā voropesi
entries.subject: yaṁ

spans.text: Na taṁ, deva, vañcemi; I am not deceiving you, “Taggha tvaṁ, mahārāja, accayo accagamā yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yaṁ tvaṁ pitaraṁ dhammikaṁ dhammarājānaṁ jīvitā voropesi.
It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to take the life of your father, a just and principled king, for the sake of sovereignty.
Evaṁ vutte, rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: When the Buddha had spoken, King Ajātasattu said to him, “handa ca dāni mayaṁ, bhante, gacchāma bahukiccā mayaṁ bahukaraṇīyā”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: When the Buddha had spoken, King Ajātasattu said to him, “handa ca dāni mayaṁ, bhante, gacchāma bahukiccā mayaṁ bahukaraṇīyā”ti.
Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantassa rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa bhikkhū āmantesi: Soon after the king had left, the Buddha addressed the mendicants: “khatāyaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā.

spans.text: If he had not taken the life of his father, a just and principled king, the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma would have arisen in him in that very seat.”
